segments.he: עָרֵב הַיּוֹצֵא לְאַחַר חִיתּוּם שְׁטָרוֹת וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב: קוֹדֶם חִיתּוּם שְׁטָרוֹת – גּוֹבֶה מִנְּכָסִים מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים. לְאַחַר חִיתּוּם שְׁטָרוֹת – גּוֹבֶה מִנְּכָסִים בְּנֵי חוֹרִין.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: In the case of «a guarantor whose» commitment «emerged,» i.e., was written, «after the signing of» the promissory «note,» the creditor can collect the debt only from unsold property of the guarantor. «Rav says:» If the guarantor’s commitment is written «before the signing of the document,» the creditor can «collect» the debt from the guarantor «from liened property» that has been sold; if it is written «after the signing of the document,» the creditor can «collect» the debt only «from unsold property.»

moves.summary: Rav distinguishes before and after signing
moves.about: the mishna's limit applies after signing; before signing the guarantor is collected from liened property

edges.about: the mishna's limit applies after signing; before signing the guarantor is collected from liened property

positions.claim: before signing: liened property; after: free property
